title: Frontend: Animated Loading Skeleton
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Animated Loading Skeleton. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Export App({state="loading",content="Ready"}). loading renders [data-testid="skeleton"] aria-hidden=true and sets region aria-busy=true. success renders content, empty renders No results, error renders Unable to load. Only loading has a skeleton. No network request is required.
constraints: Export default App. Only react and react/jsx-runtime imports are supported. The DOM contract and supplied props define the exercise.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Keep loading state explicit and reserve approximately the final layout dimensions to reduce shifts.
alternativeApproaches: Coordinate several regions so partial data can render without resetting already usable sections.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Loading to success; failure; empty response.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
